chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad and Sahl ibn Ziyad, all from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from Dawud ibn Sirhan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)

Regarding the man who has land upon which is a known tax (kharaj), which sometimes increases and sometimes decreases, so he hands it over to a man on the condition that he pays its tax and gives him two hundred dirhams in the year. He (peace be upon him) said: There is no problem.

key_terms.خَرَاج: Land tax or tribute, typically on agricultural land
key_terms.لَا بَأْسَ: There is no problem / it is permissible
key_terms.يَدْفَعُهَا: He hands it over / leases it

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to rent out land with variable tax to a tenant for a fixed annual fee?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Kafi clarifies the permissibility of a hybrid lease structure where the tenant assumes the risk of variable land tax (kharaj) while paying the owner a fixed rent, reflecting the practical economic realities of early Islamic agrarian society. It demonstrates the Imam’s flexibility in commercial contracts, distinguishing this arrangement from prohibited elements of uncertainty (gharar) by anchoring the core transaction in a known fixed sum. This ruling underscores the Shia juristic principle that variable obligations can be validly transferred in lease agreements provided the essential terms are clear.
